summary: The note describes the annual Book Drive and Literacy Day held at the local library on September 15, 2023, where community members donated and took books under the motto 'Take a Story, Leave a Story.' It highlights individual stories, such as a donated copy of The Secret Garden and A People's History of the United States, and the organizers' views on literacy. Hundreds of books changed hands, and the event was framed as a celebration of shared experiences and the hope it would continue in future years.
one_line: The annual Book Drive and Literacy Day at the local library on September 15, 2023 saw hundreds of donated books exchanged and shared stories celebrated.
key_facts: The annual Book Drive and Literacy Day took place on September 15, 2023, at the local library.
A line had already formed when the clock struck ten in the morning.
Grace Thompson, a librarian and one of the organizers, stood beside a sign reading 'Take a Story, Leave a Story.'
Grace Thompson said every book has the potential to open up entire universes, and that reading 'requires such little effort for such an expansive return.'
Laura Mitchell, a mother of two and a nurse, donated a well-thumbed copy of 'The Secret Garden' by Frances Hodgson Burnett, which she said was her companion through some of her hardest days.
A young girl soon picked up the donated copy of 'The Secret Garden.'
Retired history teacher Mr. George Franklin donated 'A People's History of the United States' by Howard Zinn.
Teenager Alex Ramirez, who has a newfound appetite for history, browsed the nonfiction section and was moved by Mr. Franklin's donation.
Alex Ramirez said books like Zinn's show there is more than one narrative to every story.
Cynthia Barnes, a veteran teacher, served as the event's coordinator and said literacy is about understanding and connection, not just being able to read.
Donations included old cookbooks, science fiction and fantasy novels, textbooks, classics, and contemporary bestsellers.
The Book Drive and Literacy Day saw hundreds of books change hands by the end of the day.
